newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel to raise shuttle prices - paper.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel to raise shuttle prices - paper.

text.p: Channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel will raise prices in March for its passenger shuttle service between France and Britain, the Financial Times reported on Thursday.
The increase signals Eurotunnel's withdrawal from a fierce price-cutting war with ferry operators.

The Financial Times said fares would rise by between 40 and 70 pounds ($64 to $112). From March, it will cost 169 pounds ($271) return for a car and up to nine passengers staying away for at least six days and 199 pounds ($319.1) at peak times.
"We are confident these are the right prices," Eurotunnel's managing director of passenger shuttle services, Bill Dix, was quoted as saying.

"We had a false market when the ferries threw extra capacity on to the Dover-Calais route, but we believe there will be a rationalisation which will allow prices to harden to some degree," Dix said. ($1=.6237 Pound)
